meta.title: Use of Safety Shower in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide immediate emergency decontamination by flushing the body with large volumes of water in the event of a chemical splash, spill, or fire involving laboratory personnel in the Pharmacognosy laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory as an emergency safety device — to be used immediately when chemical contamination of the body, skin, or clothing occurs.
procedure: In case of major chemical contamination or clothing fire: immediately walk or assist the affected person to the safety shower — do not delay.
Pull the shower handle downward (overhead pull chain or push handle) firmly to activate the water flow.
Step directly under the shower and allow the water to flow continuously over the affected area.
Remove contaminated clothing, shoes, and jewellery while standing under the shower — do not waste time removing garments before activating the shower.
Flush the affected area continuously for a minimum of 15–20 minutes as per ANSI Z358.1 standard.
Have another person call for emergency medical assistance (campus emergency / 108) immediately while the shower is running.
Do not turn off the shower prematurely — 15 minutes is the minimum even if symptoms appear to improve.
After flushing, escort the affected person to the medical facility for evaluation even if no visible injury is apparent.
After the emergency, inspect the shower: refill tank (if tank-type) or verify mains supply is restored; note the incident in the accident register.
Report the incident to the laboratory in-charge within 1 hour.
precautions: Test the safety shower weekly by activating it briefly (5–10 seconds) to confirm water flow and clear stagnant water from the pipe.
Keep the area directly under and around the safety shower completely clear of obstruction at all times — no storage of any materials.
Mark the safety shower location with high-visibility signage and floor markings visible from all parts of the laboratory.
Ensure the safety shower is within 10 seconds walking distance (approximately 10 metres) of all hazardous work areas, as per ANSI Z358.1.
Train all laboratory personnel in the location and operation of the safety shower during induction.
Do not allow the safety shower to be blocked, locked, or obstructed under any circumstances.
Record all monthly inspection dates and test activations in the safety equipment register.
Ensure drains are functional to handle the high flow rate of the safety shower (~75 litres per minute) without flooding.
